# CredMgr — knowledge base for language models

CredMgr is a local credential vault. One broker process (`credmgrd`) holds the keys and decides every request; the app, the CLI (`credmgr`) and the MCP server (`credmgr mcp`) are clients of it. The broker has no network code: nothing in the vault is sent anywhere.

This file tells a model everything it needs to drive CredMgr without the app window: the features, every setting with what it is for and where it lives, how to connect, where data is kept, and how to read and change settings through the **switchboard**.

## 1. Connect

- **Local agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, Claude Desktop):** the MCP server runs over stdio. Print the config to paste with `credmgr mcp --print-config`, or let CredMgr add itself with `credmgr agent connect <client>`.
- **Your scope:** an agent is scoped by its working folder. Start it inside a folder bound to a project; `credmgr_whoami` tells you the node you reach.
- **The vault must be unlocked by the owner** (the app, Touch ID, or `credmgr unlock`). An agent never unlocks it.
- **Cloud assistants (claude.ai, ChatGPT):** not connected in this version. The planned design keeps values on the Mac and lets a remote assistant use credentials without receiving them (`docs/26` Phase 5).

## 2. Where data lives

| What | macOS | Linux | Windows |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vault (encrypted entries, signed registry, audit log) | `~/Library/Application Support/credmgr` | `$XDG_DATA_HOME/credmgr` (`~/.local/share/credmgr`) | `%APPDATA%\credmgr` |
| State (broker socket, counters) | `~/Library/Application Support/credmgr-state` | `$XDG_STATE_HOME/credmgr` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\credmgr\state` |
| Settings | inside the signed registry: `global.policy.appPrefs`, `global.policy.revealConfirm`, `<node>.policy` | same | same |

`CREDMGR_VAULT_DIR` and `CREDMGR_STATE_DIR` override both. Values are encrypted per project; names and settings are signed so a changed file is refused.

## 3. Retention and backup

- Every write keeps the previous value; `credmgr_undo` reverses the last change to an entry. A removed entry can be restored for 7 days.
- `credmgr backup` (owner) writes an encrypted copy of the vault; `app.backupRetain` sets how many are kept. `credmgr restore` is offline.
- Every setting change made through the switchboard is recorded with its previous value and can be reverted (`credmgr_settings_revert`).
- The audit log keeps every operation, never a value.

## 4. The switchboard

| MCP tool | CLI | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `credmgr_settings_list` | `credmgr settings list [--node <id>]` | Every setting with its current value, default, scope, risk and whether **you** may change it directly or need approval. |
| `credmgr_settings_get` | `credmgr settings get <id> [--node <id>]` | One setting, described in full. |
| `credmgr_settings_set` | `credmgr settings set <id> <json> [--node <id>] --reason <why>` | Change a setting (`toggle` is `set` with the other boolean). |
| `credmgr_settings_revert` | `credmgr settings revert <change>` | Put back the value a recorded change replaced. |
| `credmgr_settings_request` | `credmgr settings requests` / `approve <id>` / `deny <id>` | An agent polls its waiting request; the owner lists and decides them. |
| `credmgr_kb` | `credmgr kb` | This file. |

### Safety tiers

- **Cosmetic** changes (appearance, layout) apply at once, for an agent too.
- **Strengthening** changes (a stricter level, a shorter lock, protection on) apply at once, for an agent too.
- **Weakening** changes (a longer or no auto-lock, a looser reveal policy, a lower security level, more agent access, protection off) from an agent become a **request**: `credmgr_settings_set` answers `state: "pending"` with a `request` id. The owner approves it on their own device after a fresh Touch ID or passphrase confirmation; the change then applies and is recorded. Poll with `credmgr_settings_request`. A request expires after 10 minutes.
- An agent sees and changes project settings only for projects in its own scope.
- Not on the switchboard (owner-only operations, unchanged): unlocking, Touch ID enrolment, second-factor enrolment, grants, creating or sealing projects, rotating the root key, deleting orphans, backups and exports.

### Examples

```json
{"tool": "credmgr_settings_set", "arguments": {"id": "app.theme", "value": "dark", "reason": "user asked for dark mode"}}
```
→ `{"applied": true, "change": "cosmetic", "changeId": "sc-…"}`

```json
{"tool": "credmgr_settings_set", "arguments": {"id": "node.securityLevel", "node": "acme", "value": "open", "reason": "user wants no approvals on acme"}}
```
→ `{"applied": false, "state": "pending", "request": "sr-…", "change": "weakens"}` — tell the user to approve it in CredMgr.

```sh
credmgr settings set app.autoLockMins 5 --reason "lock sooner"
credmgr settings list --node acme
```

## 5. Every setting

### Locking and revealing

| id | scope | values | default | risk | what it is for | where |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `app.autoLockMins` | vault | 5 \| 15 \| 60 \| 0 | `15` | higher or 0 is weaker | Locks the vault after this many minutes without activity in the app; 0 turns the idle timer off (the vault still locks on sleep, screen lock and when the window is put away). | Settings › Security › Auto-lock; stored `global.policy.appPrefs.autoLockMins` |
| `app.revealWindowSecs` | vault | 10 \| 20 \| 60 | `20` | higher is weaker | How long a revealed value stays on screen in the app before it is masked again. | Settings › Security › Reveal window; stored `global.policy.appPrefs.revealWindowSecs` |
| `app.captureProtection` | vault | true \| false | `true` | `false` is weaker | Screenshots, recordings and screen sharing show the app's window blank, on every display. | Settings › Security › Screen capture; stored `global.policy.appPrefs.captureProtection` |
| `vault.confirmBeforeReveal.mode` | vault | off \| window \| everyTime | `"off"` | weaker toward `off` | Makes the owner's own login prove a person is at the keyboard (Touch ID or passphrase) before a value is shown: once per window, or every time (ADR-150). | Settings › Security › Confirm before showing secrets; stored `global.policy.revealConfirm.mode` |
| `vault.confirmBeforeReveal.windowSeconds` | vault | 60 \| 300 \| 900 \| 3600 | `300` | higher is weaker | How long one confirmation covers further reveals when the mode is `window`. | Settings › Security › Confirm before showing secrets › Window; stored `global.policy.revealConfirm.windowSeconds` |
| `vault.confirmBeforeReveal.scope` | vault | all \| high | `"all"` | weaker toward `high` | `all` values, or only entries whose sensitivity is high or critical. | Settings › Security › Confirm before showing secrets › Covers; stored `global.policy.revealConfirm.scope` |

### Projects (nodes)

| id | scope | values | default | risk | what it is for | where |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `node.securityLevel` | node | open \| guarded \| sealed | `"guarded"` | weaker toward `open` | How much an agent may do on this project without the owner: `open` (no approvals), `guarded` (high and critical reveals wait for approval), `sealed`, shown as Strict (every reveal waits; agent creates go to the held tray). | Node inspector › agents here; stored `<node>.policy.securityLevel` |
| `node.agentAccess` | node | none \| read-only \| read-write | `"read-write"` | weaker toward `read-write` | Whether agents scoped to this project may read and write, only read, or nothing. | Node inspector › Policy; stored `<node>.policy.agentAccess` |
| `node.privateNames` | node | true \| false | `false` | `false` is weaker | Hides this project's label and entry names from everyone but the owner's login (ADR-083). | Node inspector › Policy; stored `<node>.policy.privateNames` |
| `node.requireTwoFactor` | node | never \| reveal \| always | `"reveal"` | weaker toward `never` | When this project's two-factor gate is asked for, if one is enrolled: on every read, on reveals only, or never. | Node inspector › Policy; stored `<node>.policy.requireTwoFactor` |
| `node.lockAfterSeconds` | node | 30..604800 \| null | `null` | higher or null is weaker | Locks just this project again after this many seconds unlocked; null keeps it open while the vault is. | Node inspector › Policy; stored `<node>.policy.lockAfterSeconds` |
| `node.descendantRead` | node | true \| false | `false` | `true` is weaker | Lets this project read its own sub-nodes' entries (parents do not read children unless this is on). | Node inspector › Policy; stored `<node>.policy.descendantRead` |
| `node.siblingVisibility` | node | isolated \| shared | `"shared"` | weaker toward `shared` | Whether sub-nodes under one parent read each other's entries (`shared`) or not (`isolated`). | Node inspector › Policy; stored `<node>.policy.siblingVisibility` |

| id | scope | values | default | risk | what it is for | where |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| `app.colour` | vault | off \| on \| auto | `"off"` | cosmetic | Tints the interface with the accent hue. | Settings › Appearance; stored `global.policy.appPrefs.colour` |

| `app.intensity` | vault | 0..100 | `32` | cosmetic | How strong the accent tint is, 0 to 100. | Settings › Appearance; stored `global.policy.appPrefs.intensity` |
| `app.greyscale` | vault | true \| false | `false` | cosmetic | Shows the interface without colour. | Settings › Appearance; stored `global.policy.appPrefs.greyscale` |
| `app.contrastMode` | vault | standard \| high \| null | `null` | cosmetic | Standard or high contrast; null follows the operating system. | Settings › Appearance; stored `global.policy.appPrefs.contrastMode` |
| `app.motion` | vault | system \| reduced | `"system"` | cosmetic | Follow the system's reduced-motion setting, or always reduce motion. | Settings › Appearance; stored `global.policy.appPrefs.motion` |
| `app.hwAccel` | vault | true \| false | `true` | cosmetic | Draws the graph with the GPU. | Settings › Appearance; stored `global.policy.appPrefs.hwAccel` |

| `app.entriesMode` | vault | all \| selected | `"all"` | cosmetic | List every reachable entry, or only the selected project's. | Main view; stored `global.policy.appPrefs.entriesMode` |
| `app.view` | vault | graph \| tree | `"graph"` | cosmetic | Graph or tree. | Main view › graph / tree; stored `global.policy.appPrefs.view` |

## 6. Features

| Feature | What it is for | How to use it without the app |
|---|---|---|
| **Projects (nodes) as boundaries** | Every project is a node with its own key. Everything reads Global; projects never read each other; sub-nodes read their parents. | MCP `credmgr_whoami` shows your node; CLI `credmgr node list`, `credmgr node create` (owner). |
| **Entries and fields** | A credential is an entry with one or more labelled fields; every write keeps history and can be undone. | MCP `credmgr_list`, `credmgr_create`, `credmgr_update`, `credmgr_rotate`, `credmgr_undo`; CLI `credmgr set`, `credmgr get`, `credmgr list`. |
| **Agent scoping by working folder** | An agent started in a folder bound to a project reaches that project, its ancestors and Global, nothing else. | CLI `credmgr node create <id> --workdir <dir>` (owner); MCP `credmgr_whoami`. |
| **Security levels** | Per project: open, guarded or Strict (stored as sealed) — how much an agent's request waits for the owner. | Setting `node.securityLevel` through the switchboard. |
| **Approvals** | A request the vault holds back (a guarded reveal, a weakening setting change) waits for the owner's decision on their device. | Owner: the app, or CLI `credmgr settings requests` / `credmgr settings approve <id>`; agent: MCP `credmgr_settings_request` to poll. |
| **Touch ID** | A Secure Enclave key proves a person is present for the gated operations, and can unlock the vault. Agents can never use it. | Owner only: Settings › Security › Touch ID; CLI `credmgr unlock --touch-id`. |
| **Second factor (TOTP gates)** | A vault or project can require a TOTP code before reading or revealing. | Owner only: CLI `credmgr gate enroll`; setting `node.requireTwoFactor`. |
| **TOTP codes** | An entry can hold a 2FA seed; the vault answers the current code, never the seed, to agents. | MCP `credmgr_totp_code`; CLI `credmgr totp <name>`. |
| **Encrypted backup and restore** | A backup is the encrypted vault as it is on disk; restore is offline and makes no network call. | Owner: CLI `credmgr backup`, `credmgr restore`; setting `app.backupRetain`. |
| **Encrypted export** | One project exported as an age file under a passphrase you choose. | Owner: CLI `credmgr node export <id> --age <file>`. |
| **Seal and restore** | Sealing a project moves it to Orphaned: names stay, values become owner-only until restored. | Owner: app node menu, CLI `credmgr node seal` / `credmgr node restore`. |
| **Audit log** | Every operation is recorded in a hash-chained log with no value in it. | Owner: CLI `credmgr audit`; MCP `credmgr_recent_changes` for your own scope. |
| **Changing the passphrase** | The owner can change the vault passphrase; it replaces the root key and issues a new recovery code. Agents cannot. | Owner only: Settings › Security › Passphrase; CLI `credmgr passphrase` (both values on stdin). |
| **Expiry, history and references** | An entry can carry an expiry date; the owner can list what expires soon and read one entry's trail. No value is ever in either. Every entry also has a vault-wide reference number. | Owner: CLI `credmgr expire`, `credmgr expiring`, `credmgr history`, `credmgr ref <number>`. No MCP tool. |
| **Anomaly alarm** | Five refusals across node boundaries in ten minutes raise an alarm the owner sees; an agent that keeps probing other projects is noticed. | Owner: the app's notice bar; CLI `credmgr status` shows unseen alarms, `credmgr status --ack` marks them seen. |
| **Switchboard** | Every setting in this file can be read and changed without the app window, with the safety tiers below. | MCP `credmgr_settings_*`; CLI `credmgr settings ...`. |

## 7. Every MCP tool

`credmgr_whoami` · `credmgr_list` · `credmgr_search` · `credmgr_get` · `credmgr_get_metadata` · `credmgr_create` · `credmgr_update` · `credmgr_rotate` · `credmgr_field_add` · `credmgr_field_update` · `credmgr_field_remove` · `credmgr_remove` · `credmgr_undo` · `credmgr_totp_code` · `credmgr_recent_changes` · `credmgr_settings_list` · `credmgr_settings_get` · `credmgr_settings_set` · `credmgr_settings_revert` · `credmgr_settings_request` · `credmgr_kb`

Call `credmgr_whoami` first. A tool never widens your scope; if you need something outside it, ask the user.

## 8. Rules for a model

- Prefer reading names and metadata over revealing values. A value you reveal enters your context and cannot be taken back.
- Give a `reason` for every change; it is shown to the owner and kept in the record.
- When a change answers `pending`, tell the user what you asked for and that it waits for their approval in CredMgr. Do not retry in a loop.
- Never ask the user for their passphrase, recovery code or a TOTP seed.
